text:
maya: Heads-up — canary token/sec collapsed ~30% after the last canary rollout (PR #4821). Started a rollout hold.
maya: quick screenshot: avg token/sec per pod went from 14.2k -> 9.8k over 10m. latency p95 barely moved tho.
ryan: ugh. any obvious changelist in that PR?
maya: PR touched kernel-selection and continuous-batcher pacing heuristics. notable: switched kernel-affinity heuristic to prefer memcpy-optimized path for small batches. also adjusted target_batch_ms 8 -> 14.
samir: ci-bot flagged a perf regression earlier — perf/job/742 showed -28% token/sec on the same branch.
ci-bot: perf-checker: job 742 (branch: maya/ctb-affinity) FAILED. token_sec delta = -27.9%, bench config: seq_len=64, batch_ms=10. See https://ci.example/reports/742
julie: can we repro locally with the exact bench? if token/sec drops but latency p95 stable maybe batching changed shapes.
maya: running the bench now against canary image (sha e9f3a4) — command:
```
./bench --model small --seq 64 --duration 300 --concurrency 8 --measure token/sec
```
maya: local run: baseline image (sha a1b2c3) -> 14.4k tokens/s, canary (e9f3a4) -> 10.2k tokens/s.
ryan: that narrows it. either batching window change or kernel path slower for our common batch sizes. can you dump batch-size distribution from the bench?
maya: paste: `hist: {1: 12%, 2: 18%, 4: 25%, 8: 30%, 16+: 15%}` — so small-to-mid batches dominate.
julie: interesting — memcpy-optimized kernel is slower at mid batch sizes on this GPU due to an extra copy. should show up in perf profile. can you run nvprof or our in-house tracer?
maya: ran tracer, attaching top hotspots:
```
copy_kernel: 42%
attention_kernel_v2: 35%
kv_cache_lookup: 6%
scheduler_coalesce: 9%
```
maya: compare baseline: copy_kernel 18%, attention_kernel_v2 52%
samir: so copy path got hotter. That matches kernel-affinity change.
ryan: do we have a quick runtime flag to pin kernel selection back to legacy policy?
maya: yes — runtime config `kernel_policy=legacy-copy-avoid` (works per-pool). I pushed a canary config to pin the canary pods back; starting rollout now.
oncall: started config flip on canary pool (pool-id: eu-west-2-prod-canary).
ci-bot: perf-checker: rerun queued for job 743.
julie: also suspect continuous-batcher target_batch_ms increase is inflating batch sizes into regions where copy path penalty appears. two knobs interacting.
ryan: let's bisect which change is worse: revert kernel-affinity change first, then revert batch_ms tweak if needed.
maya: running quick git bisect on the branch commits — early result: commit e9f3a4 (kernel-affinity heuristic) reproduces 28% drop; commit f4a55d (batch-ms tweak) alone shows ~8% drop.
samir: thanks — so kernel-affinity is the primary culprit.
ryan: open rollback PR for the kernel-affinity change and hold the larger rollout. tag as rollout-blocker.
maya: PR #4902 opened to revert kernel-affinity heuristic. also adding a perf test to CI that runs at seq_len=64, bench distribution to catch this.
julie: good. long-term: we should add runtime telemetry that correlates batch-size histogram with kernel path selection so we can detect cross-knob regressions earlier.
ryan: agreed. also add a canary perf check to the deployment pipeline that runs token/sec baseline for 5m.
oncall: canary config flip reverted token/sec to 14.0k in ~2 mins. Canary holding at healthy.
maya: closing hold after PR merge + canary green. I'll file a short postmortem and link the perf traces + the bisect steps.
samir: leaving a note in the incident tracker: INC-2026.
ryan: thanks everyone — good triage cadence. :thumbsup:
